verdict.label: YELLOW · Half size, A-grade only — Nvidia CEO shock reverses the tech rally
verdict.desc: Wednesday's CoreWeave-led rebound is unwinding fast. Overnight, reports that Nvidia's board is weighing ousting CEO Jensen Huang — following allegations of a second affair, one reportedly with a woman suspected of spying for China — sent NVDA down ~8% pre-market and dragged the AI complex with it. A rebound in technology stocks faded as traders confronted a leadership crisis at Nvidia; Nasdaq-100 contracts fell 1.5% while S&P 500 contracts dipped 0.8%. The VIX had collapsed 10.1% to 17.49 on Wednesday but is ticking back up pre-market. Composite gap-risk sits at 48 (MILD) and P(≥1% gap) is ~33%, just below the 35% trigger. All 3 boarded names are bearish post-earnings gaps on thin confirmation volume — and two of them (CRWV, NBIS) are AI-cloud names caught in the Nvidia downdraft. This is a half-size, A-grade-only day; validate each setup at 9:35 ET before entering, and mind the two-sided squeeze risk if the Huang story resolves favorably.

focus.jtag: Wednesday's CoreWeave-led tech rebound unwound overnight after reports that Nvidia's board is weighing ousting CEO Jensen Huang. NVDA fell ~8% pre-market, dragging Nasdaq futures ~0.9% lower and S&P futures ~0.45%. The scanner boarded 3 names — all bearish Type A gaps (CRWV, NBIS, YETI)
focus.jnote: Wednesday's relief rally was real — and overnight it reversed hard on a single-name governance shock. In the regular session, the S&P 500 jumped 1.31% to end at 7,619.38, while the Nasdaq Composite advanced 1.6% to close at 25,466.19. Apple reached a fresh all-time closing high and the fear gauge, the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX), decreased 10.1% to 17.49. Then the mood flipped: shares of Nvidia sank more than 8% in premarket trading Thursday morning as the fate of Jensen Huang hung in the balance. The New York Times reported Huang had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, VP of health care at Nvidia, who reports to Huang. Several Wall Street analysts told CNBC that if Huang is removed as CEO, the stock could fall 20%. The fallout rippled across the AI complex — shares of CoreWeave, Nebius, and IREN were down in premarket trading, giving back part of the previous session's gains. Oil eased — Brent crude futures fell 1.2% to $91.7 while WTI dropped 1.1% to $85.6 — on diplomatic-progress hopes.
focus.notdown: No clean bullish Snipers boarded today. Wednesday's breakouts (Apple at a record, the CoreWeave spike) are exactly the names now reversing on the Nvidia story — selling bull puts into a tech tape that just gave back an 8% leader overnight invites a gap through your short strike. The disciplined answer on the bullish side is to sell nothing new today and let the AI-governance dust settle.
focus.notup: The scanner boarded three bearish Type A post-earnings gaps — CRWV (A+), NBIS (A), YETI (A). All three gapped down on their own earnings and all three show guidance concerns, but every one came on very light relative volume (0.08x–0.35x, far below the 1.3x confirmation bar), which is the system's biggest red flag. Two of them (CRWV, NBIS) are AI-cloud names also caught in the Nvidia downdraft, so the bear-call lean is aligned with the macro tape — but a favorable Huang resolution could squeeze them violently. Half size, validate each at 9:35 ET.
focus.why: Why YELLOW (not GREEN)? The gap math still permits risk-taking — P(≥1% gap) ~33% is below the 35% trigger and composite 48 is MILD. But two frictions keep it out of GREEN: an unscheduled, open-ended governance crisis at the single most important AI name is exactly the kind of headline tail you cannot time or size around, and all three boarded names gapped on sub-confirmation volume, which weakens every one of them. With 3 bearish names on the board, the right posture is half size, A-grade only, validate at 9:35 ET — take the best, skip the rest, and keep every spread's DTE clear of its next print.

setups.read: The scanner boarded this bearish off the earnings reaction, but the catalyst read is at odds with the live tape. CoreWeave actually closed at $60.77 on Wednesday, up $12.04 or 24.71%, after a blowout Q3 — so the scanner's ‘gap-down + guidance cut’ tag appears to be a stale/mislabeled read versus the real move. Today the stock is reversing: shares dropped 6.37% to $56.90 in premarket, reversing part of Wednesday's 24.71% gain, dragged by the Nvidia story. Barclays lowered its target to $85 from $105 (Equal Weight). Concern: the scanner's own notes flag relative volume 0.08x, far below the 1.3x bar, and the bearish-gap logic conflicts with a 25% up-day. Verify the direction and chain on your platform before anything.

setups.read: Fresh post-earnings down-gap — and here the bearish direction matches the tape. Nebius beat but guided softly: Q3 GAAP EPS of -$0.13 and revenue of $980.8 million, a 571.3% YoY increase, yet it now expects 2026 revenue at the low end of its $3.0–$3.4B forecast while guiding 2027 to $12–$13B. The soft near-term guide plus >$40B 2027 capex spooked investors — NBIS traded at $135.86 premarket, down 12.2% from Wednesday's $154.69 close. The AI-cloud group is also caught in the Nvidia downdraft. Concern: relative volume ~0.35x is below the 1.3x confirmation bar, and the stock had rallied 15%+ into the print — a favorable AI-sentiment turn could squeeze it back up.

setups.read: The cleanest stand-alone bearish catalyst on the board — and notably not an AI name, so it's insulated from the Nvidia whipsaw. YETI beat on EPS but missed on revenue and cut guidance: revenue $509.4M vs consensus $522.2M (a 2.4% miss) with adjusted EPS $0.91 vs $0.84 (an 8.1% beat), while it now projects adjusted sales growth of about 6% (down from 7–8%) and lowered adjusted EPS to $2.90–$2.95 from $2.94–$3.00. The guidance cut drove the gap: YETI stock dropped 14%, to $37.01, ahead of the opening bell. Concern: relative volume ~0.09x is far below the 1.3x bar — the thinnest confirmation on the board. S/R layers sit just overhead (sma50 ~$42.18, gap floor $42.79).
